macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise ahead of Fed decision and Big Tech earnings
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8%, the S&P 500 rose 0.7%, and the Dow advanced 0.3% as technology shares recovered. Investors are awaiting the Federal Reserve’s policy decision and earnings from major technology companies.[1]

items.title: Fed widely expected to hold rates steady
items.summary: The Federal Reserve began a two-day meeting and is broadly expected to leave its policy rate unchanged after a 25-basis-point increase in September. Markets are also focused on upcoming U.S. GDP and PCE inflation data.[8]

items.title: Global markets mixed before central-bank decisions
items.summary: The Fed, European Central Bank, and Bank of Japan are expected to keep interest rates unchanged this week, while investors assess elevated inflation risks and the possibility of further U.S. rate increases later.[3]

items.title: Asian stocks rally on AI and Anthropic IPO optimism
items.summary: South Korea’s KOSPI rose more than 4%, Japan’s Nikkei gained 1.9%, and MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index increased 1.2% as investors responded to Anthropic’s IPO filing and upcoming technology earnings.[6]

items.title: U.S. consumer confidence improves unexpectedly
items.summary: U.S. consumer confidence increased in October for the first time in four months, with assessments of labor-market and business conditions improving.[3]

items.title: Major companies report mixed earnings and announcements
items.summary: Coca-Cola raised its full-year outlook, PayPal increased its earnings guidance despite missing revenue estimates, and JetBlue reported results while projecting deeper operating-margin pressure. Whirlpool fell sharply after reporting a quarterly loss and missing revenue forecasts.[3][7]
items.source: Bloomberg via Swissinfo; The Globe and Mail

items.title: Meta expands AI financing and Nvidia collaboration
items.summary: Meta increased its planned equity fundraising to $97.5 billion to finance AI expansion, while Nvidia and Meta announced plans to broaden their collaboration on AI models.[1][7]

items.title: Brazilian stocks remain under pressure
items.summary: Brazil’s Ibovespa fell 0.82% after plunging 13.88% in the previous session, with persistent fiscal concerns continuing to weigh on the market.[4]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $75,000 as crypto stocks slide
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell below $75,000, down more than 5% over 24 hours, before recovering above $76,000. Crypto-linked equities also declined sharply, including Circle, Coinbase and BitMine.

items.title: U.S. Senate fails to advance CLARITY crypto bill
items.summary: A procedural vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed 49–50, delaying congressional efforts to establish a clearer U.S. regulatory framework for digital assets. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said regulators may still act under existing authority.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs return to net inflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $110.34 million in net inflows on October 26, ending two consecutive sessions of outflows. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for the entire reported inflow.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs post large outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $88.58 million in net outflows on October 26, with BlackRock’s ETHA losses outweighing inflows into Fidelity’s FETH.

items.title: South Korea weighs delaying crypto tax again
items.summary: South Korea’s government is considering postponing its planned 22% tax on crypto gains for a fourth time, potentially moving implementation from January 2027 to 2029. Any delay would require parliamentary approval.

items.title: Canada proposes stablecoin regulations
items.summary: Canada opened a 60-day consultation on draft stablecoin rules that would require non-bank issuers to register with the Bank of Canada, maintain full reserves at Canadian institutions and redeem tokens within three business days. The proposal would also prohibit yield payments to holders.

items.title: FinCEN withdraws crypto mixing and unhosted-wallet proposals
items.summary: The U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network withdrew proposed rules targeting crypto mixers and transactions involving unhosted wallets, citing concerns that the measures could discourage legitimate privacy-focused activity.

items.title: Ripple receives final approval for national trust bank
items.summary: A U.S. banking regulator granted final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank, which is intended to safeguard reserves backing the RLUSD stablecoin and provide crypto custody services. The bank will not accept deposits or make loans.

items.title: Binance applies for crypto license in Brazil
items.summary: Binance submitted an application for a crypto license in Brazil ahead of a regulatory deadline, beginning a review process that does not guarantee approval.

items.title: Solana Foundation launches institutional settlement standard
items.summary: The Solana Foundation launched Solana DvP, an open-source delivery-versus-payment settlement standard developed with input from JPMorgan to support institutional financial transactions.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google announces Genie 4 world model
items.summary: Google announced Genie 4, a real-time interactive simulation model designed to generate more realistic environments with native audio. The company says limited trusted testing has begun, with broader access planned through Project Genie and developer tools.

items.title: Nvidia and Meta expand Muse AI partnership
items.summary: Nvidia and Meta announced an expanded partnership focused on improving training and inference for Meta’s Muse models and agents. The announcement was paired with Nvidia’s planned $3 billion investment in a Meta equity offering.

items.title: Oracle to offer Google TPUs through its cloud
items.summary: Oracle and Google announced that Google Tensor Processing Units will become available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, marking the first reported availability of Google TPUs on a major hyperscale cloud outside Google’s own platform.

items.title: OpenAI reports three AI-generated research results
items.summary: OpenAI presented claimed advances in mathematics, theoretical physics, and computer science, including a result that could challenge the Exponential Time Hypothesis if independently validated. External scrutiny and formal verification efforts are underway, so the claims remain unconfirmed.

items.title: Liquid AI releases LFM3 multimodal edge models
items.summary: Liquid AI launched LFM3, a family of small foundation models built around a shared 2-billion-parameter backbone. The text, vision, audio, and omni variants target efficient on-device deployment.

items.title: Google previews Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2
items.summary: Google released Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 in public preview as a high-level reasoning layer for robots. The system is designed to plan tasks, recover from errors, and coordinate multiple robots using natural-language instructions.

items.title: Anthropic files for IPO
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly filed documents for a public offering, disclosing rapid revenue growth, substantial losses, major enterprise adoption, and a governance structure intended to preserve its AI-safety mission and founder influence.

items.title: Nvidia reports faster MoE inference method
items.summary: Nvidia described a combination of specialized Humming kernels, FP8 precision, and multi-token prediction that it says increased throughput by 42.5% and reduced latency by 24.5% on a 124-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: U.S. video game spending fell 1% in September
items.summary: Circana reported that U.S. spending on video game content, hardware and accessories declined 1% year over year to $4.8 billion in September. Marvel’s Wolverine led monthly full-game sales, while NBA 2K27 became 2026’s best-selling game year to date.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero set for October 29 release
items.summary: S-Game’s action role-playing game Phantom Blade Zero is scheduled to launch on PC and PlayStation 5 on October 29, making it one of the week’s most notable new releases.

items.title: GTA VI physical edition raises ownership concerns
items.summary: Discussion around Grand Theft Auto VI has focused on its reported physical “code-in-a-box” distribution model, with players debating game preservation and the future of physical media. The game is scheduled for release on November 19, 2026.

items.title: Active Matter reportedly reaches 500,000 sales
items.summary: Gaijin’s PvPvE shooter Active Matter reportedly sold 500,000 copies across platforms, including its own launcher, within six weeks of release.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly offers voluntary exits to 60,000 staff
items.summary: A gaming news roundup reports that Microsoft is offering voluntary exits to approximately 60,000 employees, alongside updates on Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and the delay of Emberville’s Early Access launch to 2027.

items.title: Minecraft reportedly arrives natively on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Minecraft is reportedly launching natively on Nintendo Switch 2 with Vibrant Visuals and a Super Mario pack, with digital owners said to receive the upgrade at no additional cost for a limited period.

items.title: German Developer Award nominees announced
items.summary: Corsair Cove leads nominations for the Deutscher Entwicklerpreis, while Stray Fawn, Quad Head and Limbic Entertainment are nominated for Studio of the Year. The announcement also highlighted recent European esports and game-industry events.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple unveils new iPad mini with OLED display
items.summary: Apple announced a new iPad mini featuring an OLED display and a faster A20 Pro chip, marking a significant refresh of its smallest tablet line.

items.title: Apple launches new MacBook Pro and iMac models
items.summary: Apple introduced new MacBook Pro and iMac models powered by its M6 chip, including a 14-inch MacBook Pro with a reported 24-hour battery life.

items.title: Intel to acquire quantum software company Classiq
items.summary: Intel is reportedly set to acquire quantum-computing software firm Classiq for approximately $2.3 billion, expanding its position in quantum technology.

items.title: Tesla expands Cybercab production strategy
items.summary: Tesla reportedly designed the Cybercab battery pack to accommodate cheaper lithium iron phosphate cells, potentially supporting lower-cost autonomous vehicle production.

items.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to tens of thousands of employees
items.summary: Microsoft has reportedly offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible employees as it restructures its workforce and redirects investment toward infrastructure.

items.title: Cybersecurity incident disrupts New Mexico hospital operations
items.summary: A cybersecurity issue forced a New Mexico hospital to divert patients and temporarily close clinics, highlighting the continuing operational risks facing healthcare providers.
